$comment: Every Citation used by a rule resolves to one entry here (src/engine/citations.test.ts). Chapter numbers follow the common English translations (BPHS: R. Santhanam; Phaladīpikā: V. Subrahmanya Sastri; Sārāvalī: R. Santhanam); a verse is given only where it is well established. 'Later tradition' marks conventions that are widely used but have no verse in the classical texts.

works.BPHS: Bṛhat Parāśara Horā Śāstra — the foundational Parāśarī text on natal astrology.
works.Phaladīpikā: Phaladīpikā of Mantreśvara (c. 14th century), a compact manual of natal rules and yogas.
works.Sārāvalī: Sārāvalī of Kalyāṇavarmā (c. 9th–10th century), notable for its chapters on planetary combinations.
works.Sūrya Siddhānta: Sūrya Siddhānta, the classical astronomical treatise; its chapter on conjunctions defines planetary contests.
works.Muhūrta Cintāmaṇi: Muhūrta Cintāmaṇi of Rāma Daivajña (1600), the standard muhūrta text; its sixth chapter sets out the Aṣṭakūṭa.
works.Later tradition: A convention found in later manuals and commentaries rather than in a verse of the classical texts.
works.Porutham tradition (Tamil jyotiṣa): The South Indian (Tamil) practice of marriage matching by ten agreements (daśa porutham), as set out in the common Tamil almanacs and jyotiṣa manuals.
works.Sāmudrika Śāstra: Sāmudrika Śāstra — the Indian tradition of reading the body's marks; its hasta (hand) section reads the lines and fingers.
works.Cheiro, Language of the Hand: Cheiro (William John Warner), Cheiro's Language of the Hand, 1894 — a public-domain classic of Western palmistry.
works.Gettings, The Book of the Hand: Fred Gettings, The Book of the Hand, 1965 — source of the four-element hand typology (earth, air, fire, water).
works.Muhūrta tradition: The working rules of the muhūrta manuals and almanacs (Muhūrta Cintāmaṇi, Muhūrta Mārtaṇḍa and the printed pañcāṅgas) for dividing the day into choghaḍiyās, horās and named muhūrtas.

entries.title: Graha dṛṣṭi
entries.description: Planetary aspects: every graha aspects the 7th; Maṅgala also the 4th and 8th, Guru the 5th and 9th, Śani the 3rd and 10th.

entries.title: Various yogas
entries.description: Includes Gaja-Kesari (Guru in a kendra from Candra) and Amalā (only benefics in the 10th).

entries.title: Candra yogas
entries.description: Lunar yogas: Sunaphā, Anaphā, Durudharā, Kemadruma and Adhi, read from the grahas around Candra.

entries.title: Sūrya yogas
entries.description: Solar yogas: Veśi, Vāśi and Ubhayacarī, read from the grahas on either side of Sūrya.

entries.title: Rāja yogas
entries.description: Combinations of kendra and trikona lords, including the lords of the 9th and 10th together or in exchange.

entries.title: Pañca-Mahāpuruṣa
entries.description: The five great-person yogas: Maṅgala, Budha, Guru, Śukra or Śani in its own or exaltation sign and in a kendra (Rucaka, Bhadra, Haṃsa, Mālavya, Śaśa).

entries.title: Yogas
entries.description: The yoga chapter: cancellations of Kemadruma, the three kinds of Parivartana (Mahā, Khala, Dainya) and Harṣa, Sarala and Vimala (Viparīta Rāja).

entries.title: Rāja yogas
entries.description: Royal combinations, including Nīca-Bhaṅga: a graha's fall cancelled when its dispositor or exaltation lord holds a kendra.

entries.title: Two-graha combinations
entries.description: The effects of two grahas in one sign, including Sūrya with Budha (Budha-Āditya) and Candra with Maṅgala.

entries.title: Graha yuti / yuddha
entries.description: Planetary conjunctions: two star-planets within a degree are in contest; the one further north is the victor.

entries.title: Kāla-Sarpa
entries.description: All seven grahas on one side of the Rāhu–Ketu axis. Widely used in modern practice; not described in BPHS or the other classical texts.

entries.title: Kuja doṣa (Manglik)
entries.description: Maṅgala in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th from the Lagna, Candra or Śukra, as given in later muhūrta manuals.

entries.title: Exceptions to Kuja doṣa
entries.description: The standard exceptions: Maṅgala in own or exaltation sign; in the 2nd in Mithuna or Kanyā; joined or aspected by Guru; with Śani; both charts Manglik; and past the 28th year (some schools; recorded, never applied).

entries.title: Aṣṭakūṭa
entries.description: The eight kootas of Guna Milan — Varṇa, Vaśya, Tārā, Yoni, Graha Maitrī, Gaṇa, Bhakūṭa, Nāḍī — worth 1 to 8 points, 36 in all.

entries.title: Exceptions to Bhakūṭa and Nāḍī doṣa
entries.description: Commentarial exceptions: Bhakūṭa eased when the sign lords are the same or mutual friends; Nāḍī eased for the same sign with different nakshatras, the same nakshatra with different padas, or friendly sign lords.

entries.title: The ten poruthams
entries.description: Dina, Gaṇa, Mahendra, Strī-dīrgha, Yoni, Rāśi, Rāśyādhipati, Vaśya, Rajju and Vedha — each agreement either holds or does not; Rajju and Vedha are weighed heaviest.

entries.title: Exception to Gaṇa doṣa
entries.description: Commentarial exception: Gaṇa doṣa eased when the two Moon-sign lords are one graha or mutual friends, or when Bhakūṭa is free of doṣa.

entries.title: The heart line
entries.description: The line beneath the fingers, read for the temperament of affection: its length, depth and curve.

entries.title: The head line
entries.description: The line across the middle of the palm, read for the style of thinking: its length and slope.

entries.title: The life line
entries.description: The line curving around the mount of the thumb, read for vitality of temperament: the breadth of its arc and its depth.

entries.title: The fingers
entries.description: The relative lengths of the fingers, notably the index (tarjanī) against the ring finger (anāmikā).

entries.title: The thumb
entries.description: The supple-jointed thumb that bends back and the firm-jointed thumb that stands upright, read as adaptability and will.

entries.text: Gettings, The Book of the Hand
entries.title: The four elemental hands
entries.description: Earth (square palm, short fingers), air (square palm, long fingers), fire (oblong palm, short fingers), water (oblong palm, long fingers).

entries.title: Aṣṭakavarga
entries.description: The benefic places (bindus) each of the seven grahas and the Lagna contributes to every graha's Bhinnāṣṭakavarga, counted from the contributor's own sign.

entries.title: Trikoṇa-śodhana
entries.description: The trinal reduction: in each group of trinal signs the least bindu count is taken from all three; a zero leaves the group as it is.

entries.title: Aṣṭakavarga in transit
entries.description: A graha moving through a sign where its own Aṣṭakavarga holds more bindus is read as passing more smoothly; fewer bindus, as asking more care.

entries.title: The 28-bindu mark
entries.description: Manuals read a sign of the Sarvāṣṭakavarga with 28 or more bindus (about the mean of 337 ÷ 12) as supportive, and one below 25 as asking for more effort.

entries.title: Gocara-phala
entries.description: Transits are counted from the natal Moon's sign. Favourable houses: Sūrya 3, 6, 10, 11; Candra 1, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11; Maṅgala, Śani, Rāhu and Ketu 3, 6, 11; Budha 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 11; Guru 2, 5, 7, 9, 11; Śukra 1–5, 8, 9, 11, 12. A favourable transit is obstructed (vedha) by another graha in its paired house, except between Sūrya and Śani or Candra and Budha.

entries.title: Tārā-bala
entries.description: Count from the birth nakṣatra to the day's nakṣatra and reduce by nine: Janma, Sampat, Vipat, Kṣema, Pratyari, Sādhaka, Vadha, Mitra, Parama-Mitra. The 3rd, 5th and 7th are the unkind tārās; the 1st is mixed.

entries.title: Candra-bala
entries.description: The day's Moon is supportive when it transits the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th or 11th sign counted from the natal Moon's sign.

entries.title: Śani's seven and a half years
entries.description: Śani's passage through the 12th, 1st and 2nd signs from the natal Moon, about two and a half years each (rising, peak, setting), read as a season asking for patience and steady effort.

entries.title: Śani in the 4th and 8th from the Moon
entries.description: Śani's transit of the 4th (Kaṇṭaka or Ardhāṣṭama) and 8th (Aṣṭama) signs from the natal Moon, each read as a shorter stretch of the same patient tone as the Sāḍe-sātī.

entries.title: Viṃśottarī daśā
entries.description: The 120-year cycle of nine planetary periods, starting from the lord of the Moon's birth nakṣatra, each divided in proportion into antar- and pratyantardaśās.

entries.title: Choghaḍiyā
entries.description: Day and night each in eight equal parts named Amṛta, Śubha, Lābha (favourable), Cara (neutral), Udvega, Kāla, Roga (unfavourable); the day opens with the weekday lord's part, the night with the fifth weekday's.

entries.title: Horā
entries.description: Day and night each in twelve planetary hours; the first hour after sunrise belongs to the weekday lord and the rest follow the Chaldean order Sūrya, Śukra, Budha, Candra, Śani, Guru, Maṅgala.

entries.title: Brahma-muhūrta and Godhūli
entries.description: Brahma-muhūrta is the second-to-last muhūrta of the night, 96 to 48 minutes before sunrise; Godhūli, the cow-dust hour, is the ghaṭī around sunset.

entries.title: The tithi at sunrise
entries.description: A civil day takes the tithi in force at its sunrise (udaya tithi); a tithi that begins and ends between two sunrises is kṣaya and is noted beside the day it falls in.

entries.title: Mānādhyāya — measures of time
entries.description: The measures of time, among them the saura māsa: the solar month begins at a saṅkrānti, when the Sun enters a sidereal sign.
